0.headline: Annu Projects IPO to open on August 25, listing likely on September 2
0.heading: Annu Projects IPO to open on August 25, listing likely on September 2
0.intro: Annu Projects IPO | The offer comprises an entirely fresh issue of 1.76 crore equity shares.
0.body:
Annu Projects, a New Delhi-based EPC company with a special focus on underground and overhead utilities infrastructure, has finalised August 25 as the opening date for its IPO for public subscription.

The IPO comprises an entirely fresh issue of 1.76 crore equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component, according to the red herring prospectus filed with the Registrar of Companies on August 18.

The issue size has been reduced from the 2.2 crore fresh equity shares planned in the draft document filed with SEBI in June 2025. Subsequently, the capital markets regulator cleared the IPO papers in November 2025.

The price band for the offer will be announced separately in the next couple of sessions.

The issue will remain open until August 28. The IPO share allotment is expected to be finalised by August 31, while Annu Projects shares are likely to be listed on the bourses on September 2.

Annu Projects claims to be one of the diversified companies in the EPC sector, undertaking fibre optics, sewerage and gas pipeline projects. The company has completed 362 projects over the last 21 years and has 23 ongoing projects as of June 2026. Of these, four projects each are in the telecom and gas pipeline infrastructure segments, while 14 are in sewerage infrastructure.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Of the total basic contract value of Rs 1,681.4 crore, the company has completed work amounting to Rs 676.4 crore, while its outstanding order book stood at Rs 1,005 crore as of June 2026.

The infrastructure services provider will spend Rs 15.4 crore of the net IPO proceeds on the purchase of machinery and equipment. A further Rs 115 crore will be utilised for its working capital requirements, with the remaining funds earmarked for general corporate purposes.

On the financial front, the company reported a standalone profit of Rs 33 crore and revenue of Rs 241.2 crore for the fiscal year ended March 2026.

Mefcom Capital Markets has been appointed as the merchant banker to manage the Annu Projects IPO.

Meanwhile, with the Annu Projects IPO, the mainboard segment will see four maiden public issues next week, including Symbiotec Pharmalab, Hy-Tech Engineers and Skyways Air Services, all three of which will open on August 24.

1.headline: Upcoming IPOs: Augmont Enterprises, Symbiotec, Skyways Air GMPs rise up to 29% ahead of issue opening - Check details
1.heading: Upcoming IPOs: Augmont Enterprises, Symbiotec, Skyways Air GMPs rise up to 29% ahead of issue opening - Check details
1.intro: Shares of Skyways Air Services are commanding a GMP of about 29 percent.
1.body:
The grey market premium (GMP) for shares of Augmont Enterprises and Skyways Air Services has risen ahead of their initial public offerings (IPOs), while Symbiotec Pharmalab shares are commanding a flat premium, according to platforms tracking grey market activities.

Shares of Augmont Enterprises are commanding a GMP of up to 24 per cent. Investorgain quoted a GMP of Rs 190 for the shares, indicating a listing gain of 24.11 per cent. IPO Watch also quoted a GMP of 24 per cent.

Augmont Enterprises, a Mumbai-based gold and silver platform serving businesses and consumers, will open its Rs 825-crore IPO for public subscription on August 21.

The price band for the issue has been fixed at Rs 750-788 per share, valuing the company at Rs 7,200 crore.

Meanwhile, shares of Symbiotec Pharmalab are commanding a flat GMP, according to the platforms tracking grey market activities.

The Madhya Pradesh-based contract development and manufacturing organisation, backed by Rosewood Corporation and Motilal Oswal, has decided to open its maiden public issue amounting to Rs 1,757 crore on August 24.

This would be the second mainboard IPO to open next week, alongside the public issue of Skyways Air Services.

Shares of Skyways Air Services are commanding a GMP of about 29 per cent, according to grey market tracking platforms.

The Delhi-based air freight forwarding and logistics company will open its IPO for public subscription on August 24. The issue comprises a fresh issue of shares as well as an offer-for-sale (OFS).

2.headline: Gaja Capital, Lalithaa Jewellery, others: Here's how five ongoing mainboard IPOs stack up
2.heading: Gaja Capital, Lalithaa Jewellery, others: Here's how five ongoing mainboard IPOs stack up
2.intro: Gaja is the most attractive for a long-term investor. Horizon is the second choice for investors comfortable with debt and a long holding period, said an analyst
2.body:
There are currently five mainboard IPOs available for subscription and an analyst did a SWOT analysis on them and said outlook remains positive for Gaja Alternative Asset Management and Horizon Industrial Parks.

Of the five IPOs, outlook remains positive for Gaja Alternative Asset Management and Horizon. The other three Lalitha Jewellery Mart, Shankesh Jewellers and Sunshine Pictures carry earnings quality risks and are better approached cautiously, said Abhinav Tiwari, Research Analyst at Bonanza.

Gaja Alternative Asset Management is raising Rs 550 crore and will have a market value of around Rs 2,256 crore. It manages private equity funds and alternative investment funds. Revenue increased to Rs 136 crore and profit to Rs 82 crore in FY26. Debt is very low.

The main attraction is its high management fee income and strong track record. New funds could increase assets under management and future fee income. However, recurring management fees have declined, while carried interest now contributes almost half of income.

Gaja is the most attractive for a long-term investor. Horizon is the second choice for investors comfortable with debt and a long holding period, added Tiwari.

Horizon Industrial Parks is raising Rs 2,600 crore through a completely fresh issue at Rs 57-60 per share. At the upper end, its market value will be around Rs 17,300 crore. The company is backed by Blackstone and operates 45 industrial and logistics assets across 10 cities, covering 58 million sq. ft. Occupancy is strong at 93.6%, and it has around 30 million sq. ft. of land available for future development.

Revenue grew sharply to Rs 691 crore in FY26, while EBITDA increased to Rs 608 crore and the margin reached 79%. However, the company still reported a Rs 204 crore loss because finance costs were very high at Rs 539 crore. Debt stood at Rs 6,884 crore.

The IPO plans to use Rs 2,250 crore to repay debt, which should reduce interest costs and improve profitability The large development pipeline is another positive. However, high capex and continued borrowing remain risks. Also, 32 of its 45 assets were acquired from promoter entities, meaning recent growth has partly come from acquisitions, analysed Tiwari.

Lalitha Jewellery Mart is raising Rs 1,700 crore and will have a market value of around Rs 11,250 cr. It has 6l stores, mainly across South India. Revenue increased to Rs 25,024 crore in FY26 and profit reached Rs 1,010 cr.

The valuation looks cheap at around 10x earnings. However, gold volumes declined from 26,019 kg to 21,691 kg in two years. This means much of the revenue growth came from higher gold prices rather than higher sales volumes. The company also does not hedge gold prices. Cash flow was negative at Rs 398 crore, while customer advances and inventory remain high. Around Rs 999 crore of IPO proceeds will be used to buy gold inventory. Therefore, the low valuation is understandable, said Tiwari.

Shankesh Jewellers is a Mumbai-based wholesale jewellery company supplying large jewellery chains. Revenue grew to Rs 1,631 crore and profit to Rs 107 crore in FY26. Margins improved sharply, while debt to equity declined to 0.8x.

The IPO valuation is around 12.8x earnings. Debt repayment should reduce interest costs. However, the biggest concern is that margin improvement was largely helped by gains on unhedged gold inventory Operating cash flow was almost zero despite Rs 107 crore profit. The top 10 customers account for nearly 40% of revenue, while job worker attrition has increased sharply, said Tiwari.

Sunshine Pictures is a film production company. Revenue has declined for two consecutive years, falling to Rs 74 crore in FY26 from Rs 134 crore in FY24. Profit also declined to Rs 40 crore. Despite this, the IPO values the company at around 27.5x earnings.

The company has several upcoming films and web series projects, which could support growth. However, film earnings are unpredictable and depend heavily on successful releases. Negative operating cash flow and high dependence on a few projects make the risk reward unattractive, said Tiwari.
2.ai_impact_text_summary_s: An analyst's SWOT of five IPOs found Gaja Alternative Asset Management and Horizon Industrial Parks positive. However, Lalitha Jewellery Mart, Shankesh Jewellers, and Sunshine Pictures carry earnings quality risks, warranting caution.

* Analyst positive on Gaja, Horizon Industrial Parks IPOs.
* Lalitha, Shankesh, Sunshine IPOs carry earnings risks.
